addendum: Wikipedia-led tests, addendum m: pages about a book's themes as inputs to the prediction of that single book, and the single-book results split by kind of book
status: Fixed 2026-11-25 12:40 +07:00 (05:40 UTC), before any step of it ran: no theme feature had been joined to any book row, no segment had been built, and no model of this record had been fitted or scored.
parent_record: prereg/wiki_led_settings_2026-10-20.json and addenda a to l (prereg/addenda_wiki_led/); their settings apply unless changed here. The rows, library features, Wikipedia features and LightGBM settings are those of addendum l (2026-10-30_l_books_in_time.json).
fixed_by: Claude, for Khant Phyo Wai, who asked on 25 Nov 2026: "i wanted books to make themes, wikipages, not just authors and book pages, but real relevant wikipages, and their traffic and other features to predict the individual book's sales rise, together with other feature data ofc, like the past loan trends or whatever", and: "I think i want to also segment the test into book types, such as sequeled books, or books with movies, popularity levels, and other types that you cant think, for both the author + book page only test, and this new theme to individual test."
why: Single-book models so far used only the library's loan history and the book's own and its author's Wikipedia articles. Pages about the themes of books (hand-reviewed concept pages, and pages sorted into themes by an AI model) were used only to forecast whole themes. Pages linked to well-known books through Wikidata went only into the early-warning list. Whether theme pages help predict a single book's next month has never been tested. The advisor (20 Nov 2026) asked for five seeds with mean and spread, and warned against subgroup results found after the fact, so every split and rule is fixed here first.
scope: Existing books of the main set only (addendum l): the fixed random quarter of Seattle works, 43,298 works, rows by addendum l's rule, target D = ln(1 + L(t+1)) - ln(1 + M6), test years 2019 to 2026, 1,258,807 scored work-format-months (origins 2019-01 to 2026-07). The scored rows are exactly the rows of data/db/wiki_led/l_books_in_time/preds.parquet; the code stops if they differ. New books (Test B) are not part of this addendum.

A_theme_pages.book_themes: A work's themes are its narrow (level 3) and middle (level 2) themes in data/db/taxonomy_v3/work_theme.parquet, with their strengths. They come from the work's own catalogue headings, digital subject terms and Goodreads shelves, not from loans and not from Wikipedia, so they are known once the work is in the catalogue; a row exists only after the work's first loan. No feature pools other books' loans except the theme borrowing set K below, which uses the theme's borrowing up to month t only (a work not yet lent adds nothing to it).
A_theme_pages.arm_C_hand_reviewed: The hand-reviewed concept pages of Chapter 6 (624 articles chosen without looking at traffic): the stored weekly node series data/db/interest/wiki/weekly_node.parquet, levels 3 and 2 (views of the node's pages over all English Wikipedia user views). A week is valid when it is a full week (7 days, not partial) with views above 0.
A_theme_pages.arm_A_ai_sorted: The pages sorted into themes by Claude Opus (Test F): the 40,000 pages of S2 (confidence 2 or 3, daily views in data/interim/testF_views/), page-theme pairs of confidence 2 or 3 weighted 1.0 and 0.6, narrow themes from the assignments, a middle theme the sum of its narrow themes, as code/main_study/wiki_led/testF/21_series.py. Time-safe admission, new here: S2's pages were chosen by their top-500 days over the whole period, which would let a page that becomes popular later shape the series before it does. So a page enters the series used at origin t only if it was in the daily English Wikipedia top 500 (data/raw/wiki_top_daily.json, namespace rule of Test F) on at least 2 different days on or before the last day of month t (Test F's universe rule, with the days known at t). Once admitted at t, its whole past is in the series used at t, so the normal and the recent weeks use the same pages. The 40,000 cut itself still used later top-500 days; this is reported as a limit.
A_theme_pages.series_features: For each theme series and origin t, the 7 weekly features of addendum l (lvl4, r4, r1, run, dw, chg, valid4), computed by article_features() of code/main_study/wiki_led/l_books_in_time/l02_views.py, unchanged: only weeks that ended by the last day of t, normal = median of the 26 weeks before the last 4 (at least 13 needed), missing before the series' first week with views and when the last week is more than 13 days old.
A_theme_pages.book_features: For each row (work, format, origin t) and level (narrow, middle) separately, over the work's themes at that level whose series has a non-missing r4 at t: the strength-weighted mean of each of the 7 features, plus max_r4 (the largest r4 of those themes) and lasting (1 if any of them has run of 4 weeks or more at t, else 0). 9 features per level, 18 per arm (sets TC and TA). Missing when the work has no theme at that level with a feature at t.
A_theme_pages.theme_borrowing_K: Secondary only. For each row and level, over the work's themes at that level in data/db/study3/demand_panel.parquet, in the row's format: the strength-weighted mean of (a) log share at t minus the median log share of t-5 to t and (b) the mean log share of t-2 to t minus that of t-5 to t-3, months with month_ok false left out. 4 features (set K). This is the theme's own past borrowing, the library-side partner of the theme pages.
A_theme_pages.models: LightGBM with addendum l's settings and walk-forward (test years 2019 to 2026, training rows whose target month ended before January of the test year, formats pooled with fmt, cal_month categorical), target D. For each arm X in {C, A}: HMW14X (HM + W14 + X, primary), HMX (HM + X: theme pages without the book's own pages), X alone (X + fmt), HMW14X_donor and X_donor alone (placebo 1), HMW14X_lag (placebo 2), HMW14KX (with theme borrowing). Shared: HMW14K. HM and HMW14 are the stored five-seed predictions of addendum l (data/db/wiki_led/l_books_in_time/five_seeds/preds_<seed>.parquet, made by l07_five_seeds.py; seed 20261020 equals the published predictions).
A_theme_pages.placebo_1_other_theme: Another theme with similar traffic: within each arm and level, every theme with a series gets a donor theme of the same level under a different broad theme, matched on the median log weekly share over the valid weeks of 2016-01-04 to 2018-12-30 (for arm A, the series as admitted at origin 2018-12), closest first; each donor serves at most 3 themes; themes are taken in an order drawn with seed 20261125. The book's theme features are then computed from the donors of its themes, with the same strengths. If the signal belongs to the book's own themes, the real features should beat the donor's.
A_theme_pages.placebo_2_dates_moved: The theme features of each row at origin t are replaced by the same book's theme features at origin t-12 (theme dates moved 12 months later, so no later week is used); missing where t-12 has none. If the timing matters, the real features should beat the moved ones.

decisions.M1_C and M1_A (primary, theme pages add: HMW14X minus HMW14 change rank, all formats, 2019 to 2026, five-seed mean: the one-sided bootstrap p-value (share of draws at or below 0, (1 + count) / (2,000 + 1)) passes Holm's correction over the two arms at 0.05 (the smaller p at most 0.025, then the other at most 0.05), and the estimate is above 0.
decisions.M2_X (the gain belongs to the book's own: HMW14X minus HMW14X_donor change rank: 95% interval above 0.
decisions.M3_X (the timing matters): HMW14X minus HMW14X_lag change rank: 95% interval above 0.
decisions.pass: Arm X passes only if M1_X, M2_X and M3_X all pass (an intersection of tests, no further correction). If M1_X passes and M2_X or M3_X fails, the report says the gain cannot be told apart from general traffic of similar size, or from the theme's usual timing.
decisions.secondary, reported with intervals, no p: S1_X: X alone change rank above 0, and X alone minus X_donor alone. S2_X: HMX minus HM. S3_X: HMW14KX minus HMW14K (theme pages beyond theme borrowing). S4: HMW14K minus HMW14. The top-20 share that rose and the same among rows not yet risen (early warning) for HMW14X against HMW14. Every measure also by format and for 2024 to 2026.

B_segments.comparisons: Each segment is scored for three gains: L2a = HMW14 minus HM (the existing own and author page test), M1_C = HMW14C minus HMW14, and M1_A = HMW14A minus HMW14. The models are fitted on all rows (not per segment); a segment only restricts the rows scored. Within a segment group, the change rank is the Spearman correlation within each format and origin month over the group's rows, format-months with fewer than 3 rows or a constant prediction skipped, as addendum l.

families.F1_series (Khant): Among rows of works with a matched Wikidata book item (data/db/wiki_led/l_books_in_time/matches.parquet): 'in a series, known at t' if the item follows an earlier book (P155 'follows' has a value, or a P179 'part of the series' statement has a P1545 series ordinal whose leading number is 2 or more), or is followed by a book (P156) whose earliest publication date (P577) is on or before the last day of month t; else 'no series link known at t'.
families.F2_film_or_TV (Khant): Among rows of works with a matched book item: 'film or TV adaptation released by t' if the item has an adaptation (P4969 on the item, or a pair in data/db/wiki_led/adaptations.parquet) whose classes reach film (Q11424) or a screen root of code/main_study/wiki_led/71_wikidata_events.py (SCREEN_ROOTS) through P31 and P279, and whose release date is on or before the last day of month t; else 'no adaptation released by t'. Release date as in 71_wikidata_events.py: the earliest non-deprecated best-rank P577 or P580 date at month precision or finer; with year precision only, released from January of the following year.
families.F3_popularity (Khant): Tertiles of the series' (work and format) loans in the 12 calendar months before the test year, excluded months skipped. Cut within each format and test year over the series with a scored row in that year, by rank (ties by work id), three equal-count groups: low, middle, high.
families.F4_fiction: fiction, nonfiction, other (mixed or unknown), from data/db/taxonomy_v3/work_form_label.parquet.
families.F5_audience: children (children, middle grade), young adult (young adult, new adult), adult (adult, adult default), from work_audience_label.parquet.
families.F7_book_age: months since the series' first Seattle loan at origin t (h_age): under 12, 12 to 59, 60 or more.
families.F8_author_earlier_books: yes if another Seattle work with the same creator_key had its first loan (spl_works.first_ym) before this work's first loan; no otherwise; unknown when the creator is empty.
families.F9_own_article: at origin t: the book's own article has a feature; only the author's article has one; neither.
families.F10_award: Among rows of works with a matched book item: an award received (P166) with a point in time (P585) on or before the last day of month t; else none known by t.
families.F11_translated: Among rows of works with a matched book item that has a language of work (P407): no P407 value is English (Q1860), so the Seattle copy is a translation; else written in English.
families.F12_public_domain_classic: Among rows of works with a matched book item that has a publication date (P577): earliest P577 year before 1930 (in the US public domain by 2025); else 1930 or later.
families.F13_genre: The work's strongest broad theme (work_theme level 1, rank 1): 19 groups, plus 'no theme'.
families.F14_has_theme: The work has at least one narrow theme: yes, no.

B_segments.wikidata_facts: F1, F2, F10, F11 and F12 use claims fetched now (late November 2026) with wbgetentities (props claims) for the main set's matched book items, the items they point to by P156 and the adaptation items, in batches of 10 ids, at most 3 requests a second, cached (Http class of code/main_study/wiki_led/_common.py); the class walk for F2 fetches the P279 parents of the adaptation classes the same way. Every fact that can change over time is used only with a date on or before t (a later book's publication, an adaptation's release, an award); 'follows an earlier book', the language of the work and the first publication year are fixed once the book exists. Which works have a book item at all comes from Wikidata as of October 2026, the main set's known limit.
B_segments.not_included: Whether a book was on a New York Times list before t: the matching of list entries to Seattle works was built and hand-checked only for the 7,747 well-known books, which were chosen by later loans; extending it to the main set needs a new hand check, so this split is left for later.
B_segments.five_seeds: LightGBM seeds 20261020 to 20261024 for every model (HM and HMW14 reuse the stored five-seed predictions). Each gain is the mean over the five seeds; the five single-seed values, their standard deviation (n - 1), smallest and largest, and how many are above 0 are reported. Intervals: 2,000 draws of blocks of 3 consecutive scored months (seed 20261020), the five-seed mean recomputed within each draw, differences paired on the same draws.
B_segments.tests_and_correction: For each comparison (L2a, M1_C, M1_A) and each group g: (i) the gain within g; (ii) the gain within g minus the gain within the rest of the same family's rows (the other groups of that family). Two-sided p-values from the bootstrap: 2 x min(share of draws at or below 0, share at or above 0), with the (1 + count) / (2,001) rule, capped at 1. Benjamini-Hochberg at q = 0.05 within each comparison, separately over all (i) and over all (ii). A group with fewer than 36 scored months or fewer than 1,000 scored rows is reported with its numbers and marked too small to judge; it is left out of the correction and of every claim.
B_segments.wording_rule: The report lists every group of every family for every comparison, whatever it shows. It says a gain was found in group g only if (i) is above 0 with a Benjamini-Hochberg adjusted p below 0.05, and that the gain was larger (or smaller) in g than in the other books only if (ii) has an adjusted p below 0.05. Nothing else is called a difference between kinds of books. All segment results are pre-specified but none has a pass rule of its own.

data_checks: Before any model: the scored rows equal addendum l's (1,258,807 rows, same keys); the stored HM and HMW14 seed-20261020 predictions equal l04's; the change rank code reproduces the published L2a (0.0047) from the stored predictions. Data reports (counts only, no relation to loans): theme coverage of scored rows by arm and level, admitted S2 pages by year, donor matches, and the size of every segment group.
order_of_work: 1 this record, fingerprinted in prereg/README.md and made public on GitHub before any step below; 2 Wikidata facts and segment table (data only); 3 theme series and book features (data only); 4 models for the five seeds; 5 scoring and report data/reports/theme_pages_single_books.md, in plain words; 6 code and results published in a second pull request. Nothing is rerun after a result except to fix a logged coding error (prereg/DEVIATIONS.md, with UTC times).
seen_before_fixing: All earlier results: Tests A to F, addenda h to l, the five-seed reruns of 20 Nov (main set gain +0.0049 +/- 0.0002; new books +0.0230 +/- 0.0006), the theme-level results of the concept pages (Chapter 6, about 9 to 11% more borrowing after lasting rises), of the AI-sorted pages (+1.8% and +2.9%, Test F and addendum h) and of the theme forecasts (Appendix D). For sizing only: the shapes of the stored tables; 1,258,807 scored rows from 34,813 works; 3,934 distinct matched book items, 463 of them in adaptations.parquet; 1,943 main-set works in events.parquet (the well-known books); counts of the form and audience labels over all Seattle works; the number of themes with a series in each arm (C: 242 narrow and 86 middle; S2: 241 narrow and 86 middle). No theme feature, segment label or model output of this record existed when it was fixed.
known_limits: The S2 pages were picked by top-500 days over the whole period (the admission rule removes most but not all of this). The concept pages of arm C were chosen in October 2026 from the themes' meaning, not from traffic, but by someone who knew Chapter 6's theme results. The AI sorting agreed with Khant's own labels only about 0.4 on 31 pages (data/reports/hand_check.md). Wikidata coverage limits F1, F2 and F10 to F12 to works with a matched book item. A segment result describes the rows of that group in the main set and is not a causal effect of the book's kind.
